department.name: City of Portsmouth Recreation Department
department.hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm
department.what: Runs the city's recreation centers, indoor and outdoor pools, athletic fields, boat launch, skate park, senior center, and youth, adult and senior programs. Parks, gardens and playground construction are handled by the Parks and Greenery Division of Public Works.

registration.label: Register for programs (MyRec)
registration.note: MyRec is used for registration, receipts, schedules, memberships, boat launch passes and Four Tree Island pavilion reservations. Waitlists fill residents first, then nonresidents.

projects.title: Prescott Park Project (Master Plan Phase 1A, revised 2026)
projects.summary: DPW presented a revised plan to the City Council on April 20, 2026 that would relocate and raise the Shaw Warehouse, Player's Ring and garage addition, rebuild the lean-to, replace Water Street with head-in parking, and add ADA walkways and drainage upgrades. The work implements the 2017 Prescott Park Master Plan and responds to flooding from the December 2022 storm surge.
projects.cost: FY22 CIP listed $2.925M for Prescott Park facilities capital improvements, including $1.05M from PPP; no current budget on the project page

projects.title: South Mill Pond Playground replacement, Phase 2
projects.summary: Phase 1 replaced the playground with a universal-design, ADA-compliant playground; construction started September 29, 2025 and a ribbon-cutting was held December 1, 2025. Phase 2 will add ADA-compliant restrooms in place of the porta-potties and an upgraded parking lot.
projects.cost: Included in the FY25 capital budget; no figure listed

projects.title: Chris Rice Skateboard Park Phase II
projects.summary: The skate park at 305 Greenland Road opened December 21, 2023 after the Council authorized up to $1,083,500 in bonds in April 2023. The city page says FY28 and FY29 funding covers design and construction of Phase II.
projects.cost: Phase I bond up to $1,083,500 (April 2023); Phase II in FY28 and FY29

projects.title: Athletic Fields Project (Campus Drive), Phases II and III
projects.summary: The city bonded up to $3.4 million in July 2018 for a multi-field complex on about 50 acres between Campus Drive and the DPW yard on Peverly Hill Road. Phase I built a synthetic turf field with lights and stormwater treatment; Phases II and III call for second and third fields and a new transfer station.
projects.cost: Bond up to $3.4 million (2018) plus about $1.6 million previously set aside

projects.title: Citywide Park Improvements (CIP)
projects.summary: An annual $100,000 capital line for furnishings, signage, drainage, walkways, landscaping and lighting in parks such as Sagamore Creek, Goodwin Park, Aldrich Park and Vaughan Mall. The FY22 CIP page also lists a $20,000 annual tree replacement program.

projects.title: Comprehensive Recreational Needs Study (2023 update)
projects.summary: Placework and Horsley Witten Group updated the 2010 needs study with two public workshops in 2022 and a City Council presentation on March 7, 2023. The report guides which facilities and programs the city should add or change.
